content.comment_body: I need assistance. A customer wants to use a four-position switch to create a four-stage analog output: 5V for position 1, 6V for position 2, 7V for position 3, and 8V for position 4. They also want the ability to change these values as needed from the front panel. I've shared an example using two analog outputs but haven't figured out how to do it with only one. Any guidance would be appreciated.

Hello [user_name], you need to enable the analog multiplexer. Right-click on the inputs of the analog multiplexer, select the top input, and choose "invert connector." This should make your program work. Regards
Thanks for the advice, it's working now. However, I need the solution to use just one analog output.

Hello [user_name], I've updated your basic program to address your requirements. I've also added two demo programs to give you more ideas for your project. Note: When copying and pasting an analog multiplexer function, parameter links (pointers to other functions) may be lost, so you'll need to reassign them. Feel free to ask if you need further help. Best regards [user_name]

Hello [user_name], I have a second version for you with correct values and a ramp function, so the analog output transitions smoothly between values at a defined speed instead of jumping instantly. Since I'm not sure about the specific type or behavior of your digital inputs, there could be undefined states when switching. Best regards [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Participants discussed how to set up a controller to interpret four digital inputs from a rotary switch as a single analog output with four voltage levels, with user-adjustable setpoints from the front panel. Issues included multiplexing analog signals and handling lost settings when duplicating functions. Iterative feedback and shared demo programs led to a working solution.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks to control multiple analog voltage levels using only one analog output, with digital inputs determining the output, and the ability to easily adjust voltage values through front panel controls.
